notes.decision: Translated 'they satisfied/sated her' from ⲧⲥⲓⲟ 'feed, fatten, satisfy' (Crum 397) with 3sg.f object. The Lyc form ⲧⲥⲁⲓⲟⲥ → ⲧⲥⲁⲓⲁⲥ shows regular vowel adjustment. Object 'her' likely Hyle/Error, glutted by those whom Error chose. Alternative readings (ⲧⲥⲁⲓⲟ 'adorn, honor' or ⲧⲥⲁⲃⲟ 'teach') are possible but the affliction-context favors the gluttonous-feeding sense.

Read as 'who has inundated upon them with [her] shadow.' The instrumental ⲛ̄ governs 'shadow' as the means by which Hyle floods the elements. The Greek κατακλύζω in Coptic uniformly takes ⲁ- (acc.) for what is flooded; ⲁⲭⲱⲩ 'upon them' marks the flooded objects (men/elements), and ⲛ̄ⲧⲉⲥϩⲁⲓⲃⲉⲥ 'with her shadow' marks the inundating substance. Direct correspondence: Hyle's shadow IS the cosmic flood that destroys crops.

Translated 'second-instance' rather than 'Monday' or simply 'second.' Greek δευτέρα can mean both 'second day = Monday' and 'second-(instance).' In the immediate parallel structure (ⲙⲩⲥⲧⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ // ⲇⲉⲩⲧⲉⲣⲁ), the question asks of which heavenly mystery, or of which 'second-instance' (= heavenly counterpart, cf. accumulated ⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ 'second-instance' as the technical Manichaean term for earthly enactments of heavenly mysteries) Sunday is the earthly sign. The Manichaean correspondential schema strongly favors 'second-instance' over calendrical 'Monday.'

Translated 'wears upon them' though etymology is uncertain. The verb governs the Five Garments (ⲧⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ϩⲃ̄ⲥⲱ) with the First Man as subject. Most plausible analyses: (a) ⲧⲱⲱⲙⲉ 'join, touch' with 3pl object = 'has them joined to him' (i.e., wears as armor); (b) ⲧⲱϩⲙ̄ 'summon, call' with 3pl object = 'summons them' (cf. ⲧⲁⲍⲙ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ in glossary). Both fit Manichaean cosmology of the First Man's Five Sons donned as light-armor. 'Wears' captures the garment-context most directly.

Rendered literally 'the five (and) the five times' preserving the doubled pentad-structure. ⲡⲓⲧⲟⲩ = 'the five' (cf. ⲡϯⲟⲩ in glossary); the second ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩ may be a parallel 'five' (the doublet pentad of Light, e.g. Five Sons of First Man + Five Sons of Living Spirit), or possessive 'of theirs.' ⲛ̄ⲥⲁⲡ = 'times, seasons.' Without complete context the precise structure is uncertain; the literal rendering preserves the numerical-doubling that pervades Manichaean enumerations.

Rendered tentatively 'their (own)' as a possessed feminine collective. Etymology uncertain — possibilities include: (a) Lyc plural of ⲉⲓⲱⲧ 'father' = 'their fathers'; (b) Lyc form of ⲧⲟⲩⲱⲏ 'their night' (cf. glossary); (c) ⲧⲟⲩⲏⲧⲉ as a feminine collective with ⲧⲟⲩ- prefix. Given the lacuna-laden context, no decisive reading is possible.
